This page is generated from the definitions `dima` itself parses, so every option, value and default on it is the one `dima --help` shows for this version. It also lists what the help does not show: the meaning of each value, the spellings `dima` accepts without showing them, and the environment variables behind some options. Run `dima <command> --help` for the same texts in a terminal; `-h` shows one-line summaries. Option values are lower case and case-sensitive, except those of `--color`.

| Exit status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success (also when a reader of standard output, such as `head`, stops early) |
| `1` | Internal error (a bug; please report it) |
| `2` | Usage error: invalid options, a name DiMA cannot write, two outputs on one file, a folder given as a file; also `dima` without arguments |
| `3` | Input/output or system error (missing file, no permission, disk full, a thread the system refused) |
| `4` | Invalid input data (not an aligned FASTA, unequal lengths, invalid characters in strict mode; a results file of another major schema version, or edited or damaged) |
| 128 + N | Interrupted by signal N: `130` SIGINT (Ctrl-C), `143` SIGTERM, `129` SIGHUP; on Linux also `138` SIGUSR1, `140` SIGUSR2, `142` SIGALRM, `152` SIGXCPU (on macOS SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 give `158` and `159`). Unfinished files are removed, never left partial; standard output may hold a partial document |

See [Exit codes](/reference/exit-codes/) for examples and scripts.

## `dima`

DiMA quantifies the diversity of viral protein or nucleotide alignments: for every k-mer position it counts the distinct k-mers, estimates their Shannon entropy with a correction for sample size, classifies variants into Index, Major, Minor and Unique motifs, and reports their incidence, optionally stratified by FASTA header metadata. On request it also computes their similarity-weighted entropy (Wu 2025), which is not corrected for sample size. Conserved stretches (historically conserved sequences) are reported separately.

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607); Wu 2025, Section 2.1 and Supplementary File 1, [doi:10.1093/ve/veaf029](https://doi.org/10.1093/ve/veaf029)

```text
dima [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]
```

### Options

#### `--licenses`

Print the licences of DiMA and its components, and exit

### Global options

#### `--color <WHEN>`

Controls when to use color

- Values:
  - `auto`
  - `always`
  - `never`
- Default: `auto`
- Environment: `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `CLICOLOR` (see [Environment variables](/reference/environment/))

#### `-q, --quiet`

Print errors only: no warnings, notes, progress, summary line, Cite: line or --validation report table. Errors, including the message of an interrupted run, are always printed. Giving it twice is the same as once.

#### `-v, --verbose`

Print more on standard error. With 'dima analyze', -v adds: the number of worker threads and where it came from (a scheduler's allocation can name this host, as in PE\_HOSTFILE\[node12\]=8), a note when OMP\_NUM\_THREADS is lower (DiMA does not use it), informational notes (note\[...\]), 'wrote FILE (SIZE)' for each file written and, before the summary line, the time of each phase (with a note when reading the input limited the run), the CPU time and the peak memory. Where standard error cannot redraw a line, -v also prints the phase lines of --progress plain. -vv adds debugging messages, and prints plain progress lines instead of the redrawn line on a terminal. With view, hcs, cite and completions, -v adds nothing and -vv adds debugging messages. DIMA\_LOG accepts a tracing filter such as 'dima\_core=debug', which replaces the level -q and -v choose.

- Environment: `DIMA_LOG` (see [Environment variables](/reference/environment/))

### Help and version

Every command also takes these options.

#### `-h, --help`

`-h` prints a one-line summary of each option, `--help` the full texts shown on this page. `dima help` and `dima help COMMAND` print the same as `dima --help` and `dima COMMAND --help`. Help is printed on standard output, with status 0.

#### `-V, --version`

Prints the version, such as `dima 1.2.0`, and exits with status 0. After a subcommand it names that subcommand: `dima analyze --version` prints `dima-analyze 1.2.0`.

## `dima analyze`

Analyse an alignment

Also accepted as `dima analyse`.

```text
dima analyze [OPTIONS]
```

### Input

#### `-i, --input <FASTA>`

Aligned FASTA file (plain, .gz, .bz2 or .zst; '-' or omitted = standard input)

#### `-a, --alphabet <ALPHABET>`

Sequence alphabet. 'auto' detects it from the residues of the first records with the rules of Easel's esl\_abc\_GuessAlphabet (Easel is the sequence library of HMMER, Eddy 2011); when the rules do not decide, DiMA stops and asks for this option instead of guessing. T and U are folded to the alphabet's letter; lower case is folded to upper case. Symbols: gaps - . \_, missing \~ ?, stops \* $ ^, frameshift #, and ambiguity codes (protein X B J Z; nucleotide R Y K M S W B D H V N, the IUPAC-IUB codes, and X and I, which DiMA also reads as ambiguous) exclude the k-mers that contain them; protein U (selenocysteine) and O (pyrrolysine) are residues.

**References:** Eddy 2011, [doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002195](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002195); Cornish-Bowden 1985, [doi:10.1093/nar/13.9.3021](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/13.9.3021); Los Alamos HIV Sequence Database 2009, <https://www.hiv.lanl.gov/content/sequence/HelpDocs/IUPAC.html>; Los Alamos HIV Sequence Database 2024, <https://www.hiv.lanl.gov/content/sequence/GENE_CUTTER/cutter-help.html>; Böck et al. 1991, [doi:10.1111/j.1365-2958.1991.tb00722.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2958.1991.tb00722.x); Srinivasan et al. 2002, [doi:10.1126/science.1069588](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1069588)

- Values:
  - `auto`: Detect from the data
  - `protein` (also accepted: `aa`, `amino-acid`): Amino acids
  - `dna` (also accepted: `nucleotide`): DNA
  - `rna`: RNA
- Default: `auto`

#### `--validation <MODE>`

How characters outside the alphabet are handled. 'strict' stops at the first one with its record, line and column; 'permissive' excludes the k-mers that contain them and reports one aggregated warning; 'report' is permissive and also prints the table of every character found. Structural problems (no FASTA, unequal lengths, NUL bytes) always stop the run. Default: strict.

- Values:
  - `strict`: Stop at the first character outside the alphabet
  - `permissive`: Exclude k-mers with such characters and warn
  - `report` (also accepted: `report-only`): Permissive, and print the character table

### Method

#### `-k, --kmer-length <K>`

Length k of the overlapping windows (k-mers). Default: 9 for proteins (the length of peptides presented by HLA class I molecules) and 27 for DNA/RNA (the codons of a 9-mer). Any value from 1 to the alignment length is accepted.

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607); Falk et al. 1991, [doi:10.1038/351290a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/351290a0); Rammensee 1993, [doi:10.1146/annurev.immunol.11.1.213](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.immunol.11.1.213)

#### `-s, --support-threshold <T>`

Support threshold T. A position's support N is the number of sequences with a valid k-mer there. Positions with support above T are eligible: they enter the summary statistics. With the paper's estimator ('dima'), an eligible position's entropy is corrected for sample size where possible. The correction needs at least five points (the full data set included; a minimum taken from DiMA v5.0.9, which the paper does not state), so an eligible position is corrected only when its support is at least 1.25 T (125 sequences for T = 100). With support between T and 1.25 T, and in the one tiny case T = 2, N = 3, it keeps its observed entropy; such positions are still eligible and in the summaries. Positions with support 0 (NS), below T (LS) or equal to T (ELS) are labelled and excluded from the summaries; with 'dima' LS and ELS keep their observed entropy. NS has no entropy (null, NA), where the paper assigns a pseudo-entropy of 0: a value that was not observed is missing, not zero. Default: 100, as in the paper.

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, Methods and Fig. 2, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607); Rubin 1976, [doi:10.1093/biomet/63.3.581](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/63.3.581); Silverman et al. 2020, [doi:10.1016/j.csbj.2020.09.014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csbj.2020.09.014)

#### `--estimator <ESTIMATOR>`

Entropy estimator. At a position, N is its support (the sequences with a valid k-mer there) and D the number of distinct k-mers, the Index included. 'dima' is the paper's correction: the entropies of subsamples of R% of the sequences, n = R\*N/100 rounded up, are regressed on 1/n and the intercept is the estimate, where R is every multiple of 5 from 50 to 95 that is at least 100\*T/N, plus 100%. It is the intercept expected over the paper's random with-replacement subsampling, computed exactly, so results are reproducible bit for bit; it is the limit of averaging many random subsets, as in the original method. The correction needs at least five points (the full data set included; a minimum taken from DiMA v5.0.9, which the paper does not state), so an eligible position is corrected only when its support is at least 1.25 T (125 sequences for T = 100). With support between T and 1.25 T, and in the one tiny case T = 2, N = 3, it keeps its observed entropy; such positions are still eligible and in the summaries. Positions with support up to T keep their observed entropy too. 'chao-wang-jost' (the least biased estimator in its authors' comparison) and 'miller-madow' (which adds (D - 1)/(2N ln 2)) correct every position with at least 2 sequences, low-support ones included; with 1 they give its observed entropy, 0. 'raw' is the observed (plug-in) entropy everywhere. Default: dima.

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, Fig. 2, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607); Shannon 1948, [doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x](https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x); Rao 1945; Blackwell 1947, [doi:10.1214/aoms/1177730497](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177730497); Khan et al. 2017, [doi:10.1186/s12920-017-0301-2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-017-0301-2); Chao et al. 2013, [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12108](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12108); Miller 1955; Paninski 2003, [doi:10.1162/089976603321780272](https://doi.org/10.1162/089976603321780272)

- Values:
  - `dima`: The paper's correction (exact expectation)
  - `chao-wang-jost`: The estimator of Chao et al. (2013)
  - `miller-madow`: Miller-Madow
  - `raw` (also accepted: `plug-in`): Observed (plug-in) entropy

#### `--similarity-weighted-entropy`

Similarity-weighted entropy (Wu 2025) weights each variant's entropy term by how dissimilar it is to the other variants at the position, so near-identical variants count for less. The similarity of two k-mers is the share of their k residues that are the same, (k-d)/k when they differ at d of them; every substitution counts alike. Also reported: observed and similarity-weighted entropy divided by log2 of the number of distinct k-mers (Index included), between 0 and 1; these normalised values are undefined with one distinct k-mer. All three depend on k and the alphabet.

Published in 2025 and applied in its source study only to nucleotide sequences: simulated populations, a viroid mutant pool and the populations it gave within single plants, and one plant-virus dataset; its use on amino-acid k-mers and on sequences from many hosts is dima's extension.

None of the three values is corrected for sample size: observed entropy is lower on average with fewer sequences (Zhao & Illingworth 2019, Section 3.1), similarity-weighted entropy also changes with the number of sequences (see the methodology page, Entropy and its correction), and normalised entropy also depends on sample size (Gregori et al. 2014, Sections 2.4 and 3.2). The values are written only to the results (JSON, JSONL) and the positions table, and are null (NA) without this option.

**References:** Wu 2025, Section 2.1 and Supplementary File 1, [doi:10.1093/ve/veaf029](https://doi.org/10.1093/ve/veaf029); Grishin 1995, p. 675, [doi:10.1007/BF00175826](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00175826); Zhao & Illingworth 2019, Section 3.1, [doi:10.1093/ve/vey041](https://doi.org/10.1093/ve/vey041); Gregori et al. 2014, Sections 2.4 and 3.2, [doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btt768](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btt768)

#### `--min-coverage <X>`

Flag positions whose estimated sample coverage (the probability that one more sequence carries an already-seen k-mer) is below this value, between 0 and 1. Coverage is estimated with Chao and Jost's formula and, where no k-mer is seen exactly twice, with the form of Chao, Wang and Jost. It is always reported; this option only adds the flag and a warning.

**References:** Chao & Jost 2012, Eq. 4a, [doi:10.1890/11-1952.1](https://doi.org/10.1890/11-1952.1); Chao et al. 2013, Materials and methods, [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12108](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12108)

### Metadata

#### `--query-name <NAME>`

Name of the analysed protein or gene. Default: the input file name without its FASTA and compression extensions; 'Unknown Protein/DNA/RNA' for standard input, /dev/stdin and process substitution (\<(...)).

- Also accepted: `--name`

#### `--header-format <FIELDS>`

Names of the '\|'-separated fields of the FASTA headers, e.g. 'Accession\|Host\|Country\|Year'. Variants are then counted per value of each field. Values are cleaned (invisible characters removed, white space trimmed, Unicode NFC) and empty values get the fill value.

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607); UAX #15, <https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/tr15-57.html>; Phillips 2021, <https://www.w3.org/TR/2021/NOTE-charmod-norm-20210811/>

#### `--metadata-fields <FIELDS>`

The header fields to stratify variants by (default: all fields of --header-format), e.g. 'Host\|Year'. Identifier-like fields (such as accessions) multiply the size of the results; DiMA warns about them.

#### `--header-fillna <VALUE>`

Value used for empty header fields and for headers whose field count differs from --header-format (permissive mode). Default: Unknown.

### Output

#### `-o, --output <PATH>`

Write the results here ('-' = standard output). The format follows -O or the file extension: .json, .jsonl/.ndjson or .tsv/.tab, optionally followed by .gz or .zst for compression; a name without one of these extensions needs -O. A name that asks for another compression (.bz2, .xz, .zip, ...) or for two, or that is a folder, is refused before anything runs. Without -o or --tsv-dir (with 'dima analyze', also --hcs-output), JSON goes to standard output. Files are replaced atomically, and never one that another output, the run report or the input already uses.

#### `-O, --output-format <FORMAT>`

Format of -o: 'json' (complete results with provenance), 'jsonl' (one position per line) or 'tsv' (one table; choose it with --table). Must agree with the file extension.

- Values:
  - `json`: Complete results
  - `jsonl`: One position per line
  - `tsv`: One table (see --table)

#### `--table <TABLE>`

The table written by -O tsv: positions, variants, metadata or hcs. Tables are tidy (one row per observation), tab-separated with RFC 4180 quoting, and use NA for undefined or not computed values.

**References:** Wickham 2014, [doi:10.18637/jss.v059.i10](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v059.i10); Broman & Woo 2018, [doi:10.1080/00031305.2017.1375989](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375989); RFC 4180, [doi:10.17487/RFC4180](https://doi.org/10.17487/RFC4180)

- Values:
  - `positions`: One row per position
  - `variants`: One row per variant
  - `metadata`: One row per variant and header value
  - `hcs`: One row per conserved region

#### `--tsv-dir <DIR>`

Write all four tables to this folder (created if needed) as NAME.positions.tsv, NAME.variants.tsv, NAME.metadata.tsv and NAME.hcs.tsv. NAME is the query name made safe for file names: characters other than Unicode letters, digits, '.', '-' and '\_' become '\_', leading and trailing '.' and '\_' are removed, and an empty name becomes 'dima'. With 'dima analyze' the query name is --query-name, else the input file name without its FASTA and compression extensions, and 'dima' for standard input, /dev/stdin and \<(...). With 'dima view' it is the query name in the results ('Unknown\_Protein' for results analysed from standard input).

#### `--pretty`

Indent JSON output (it is compact by default, and indented when written to a terminal).

#### `--run-report <PATH>`

Also write a run report here: version and build target, the command (file names only), status, start and end time (UTC), threads and where their number came from, platform, time per phase, CPU time, peak memory, and the size and SHA-256 of the input and of every output written. It is separate from the results, which stay identical from run to run, and holds no host or user names and no paths. It is always JSON, compressed when the name ends in .gz or .zst; a name that asks for a TSV table, JSON Lines or another compression, or that is a folder, is refused. '-' writes it to standard output when no other output goes there. It is checked and opened before anything runs, and written even when the run fails or is interrupted.

**References:** Taschuk & Wilson 2017, Rule 10, [doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005412](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005412); Khan et al. 2019, [doi:10.1093/gigascience/giz095](https://doi.org/10.1093/gigascience/giz095); Leo et al. 2024, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0309210](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0309210)

### Conserved sequences

#### `--hcs-output <PATH>`

Also write the historically conserved sequences here. The name gives the format: .json or .tsv, optionally followed by .gz or .zst. A file name with neither gets JSON, with a warning (output\_format\_assumed); standard output and other streams get JSON. A name that asks for JSON Lines, for another compression (.bz2, .xz, ...) or for two, or that is a folder, is refused. Consecutive positions whose most common (Index) k-mer reaches --hcs-min-incidence are joined when the k-mers overlap or abut; regions that include positions with support at most T (the support threshold of the analysis) are flagged, and each region reports the lowest per-position exact 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound among its members.

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607); Abd Raman et al. 2020, [doi:10.7717/peerj.7954](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.7954); Hu et al. 2013, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0059994](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0059994); Clopper & Pearson 1934, [doi:10.1093/biomet/26.4.404](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/26.4.404)

#### `--hcs-min-incidence <PERCENT>`

Minimum Index incidence (%) of the positions that form conserved sequences, above 50 and at most 100 (above 50% the Index k-mer is unique): a decimal number such as 95 or 99.5, with at most 9 decimal places and no % sign or exponent, compared exactly. Default: 100, the paper's (every sequence with a valid k-mer has the Index).

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, Methods, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607)

#### `--hcs-eligible-only`

Build conserved sequences from positions with support above T only, where T is the support threshold of the analysis (recorded in the results); positions with support at most T end a region instead of being flagged.

**References:** Hu et al. 2013, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0059994](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0059994); Castresana 2000, [doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a026334](https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a026334)

### Run

#### `-t, --threads <N>`

Worker threads. Default: RAYON\_NUM\_THREADS if set, otherwise the CPUs this process may use, limited to the CPUs granted by Slurm, PBS, SGE or LSF when running under one. Results do not depend on the number of threads.

- Environment: `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`, `SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE`, `PBS_NUM_PPN`, `PE_HOSTFILE`, `LSB_MCPU_HOSTS` (see [Environment variables](/reference/environment/))

#### `--progress <WHEN>`

How progress is shown on standard error. 'auto': on a terminal that can redraw a line, one line updated in place; elsewhere nothing, or plain lines with -v. 'plain': appended lines, one per phase and the progress at most every 10 seconds (at each 10%) and at least once a minute; recommended with screen readers, which read every update of a redrawn line, and for log files. 'off': nothing. -q always hides progress. Without this option: 'off' when DIMA\_NO\_PROGRESS is set to anything but an empty value, 0, false, no, off, n or f; otherwise DIMA\_PROGRESS (auto, plain or off; for example DIMA\_PROGRESS=plain in a shell profile), where an empty value counts as unset; otherwise 'auto'. Values are lower case, as for every option but --color.

- Values:
  - `auto`: On a terminal, one line redrawn in place; elsewhere nothing, or plain lines with -v
  - `plain`: Appended lines: one per phase, and the progress at most every 10 seconds (each 10%), at least once a minute. For screen readers and log files
  - `off`: Nothing
- Environment: `DIMA_PROGRESS`, `DIMA_NO_PROGRESS` (see [Environment variables](/reference/environment/))

### Also accepted

Not shown by `--help`; kept for older scripts.

- `--no-progress`: The same as \`--progress off\` (kept for scripts written before \`--progress\`)

Global options (`--color`, `-q`, `-v`) and `-h`/`--help`, `-V`/`--version` apply to every subcommand; see [`dima`](#dima).

## `dima view`

Convert results (JSON) to JSON, JSONL or TSV

```text
dima view [OPTIONS] --input <RESULTS>
```

### Options

#### `-i, --input <RESULTS>`

Results written by \`dima analyze\` (JSON, optionally .gz or .zst; '-' = standard input)

#### `-o, --output <PATH>`

Write the results here ('-' = standard output). The format follows -O or the file extension: .json, .jsonl/.ndjson or .tsv/.tab, optionally followed by .gz or .zst for compression; a name without one of these extensions needs -O. A name that asks for another compression (.bz2, .xz, .zip, ...) or for two, or that is a folder, is refused before anything runs. Without -o or --tsv-dir (with 'dima analyze', also --hcs-output), JSON goes to standard output. Files are replaced atomically, and never one that another output, the run report or the input already uses.

#### `-O, --output-format <FORMAT>`

Format of -o: 'json' (complete results with provenance), 'jsonl' (one position per line) or 'tsv' (one table; choose it with --table). Must agree with the file extension.

- Values:
  - `json`: Complete results
  - `jsonl`: One position per line
  - `tsv`: One table (see --table)

#### `--table <TABLE>`

The table written by -O tsv: positions, variants, metadata or hcs. Tables are tidy (one row per observation), tab-separated with RFC 4180 quoting, and use NA for undefined or not computed values.

**References:** Wickham 2014, [doi:10.18637/jss.v059.i10](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v059.i10); Broman & Woo 2018, [doi:10.1080/00031305.2017.1375989](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375989); RFC 4180, [doi:10.17487/RFC4180](https://doi.org/10.17487/RFC4180)

- Values:
  - `positions`: One row per position
  - `variants`: One row per variant
  - `metadata`: One row per variant and header value
  - `hcs`: One row per conserved region

#### `--tsv-dir <DIR>`

Write all four tables to this folder (created if needed) as NAME.positions.tsv, NAME.variants.tsv, NAME.metadata.tsv and NAME.hcs.tsv. NAME is the query name made safe for file names: characters other than Unicode letters, digits, '.', '-' and '\_' become '\_', leading and trailing '.' and '\_' are removed, and an empty name becomes 'dima'. With 'dima analyze' the query name is --query-name, else the input file name without its FASTA and compression extensions, and 'dima' for standard input, /dev/stdin and \<(...). With 'dima view' it is the query name in the results ('Unknown\_Protein' for results analysed from standard input).

#### `--pretty`

Indent JSON output (it is compact by default, and indented when written to a terminal).

Global options (`--color`, `-q`, `-v`) and `-h`/`--help`, `-V`/`--version` apply to every subcommand; see [`dima`](#dima).

## `dima hcs`

Compute historically conserved sequences from results

```text
dima hcs [OPTIONS] --input <RESULTS>
```

### Options

#### `-i, --input <RESULTS>`

Results written by \`dima analyze\` (JSON, optionally .gz or .zst; '-' = standard input)

#### `--hcs-min-incidence <PERCENT>`

Minimum Index incidence (%) of the positions that form conserved sequences, above 50 and at most 100 (above 50% the Index k-mer is unique): a decimal number such as 95 or 99.5, with at most 9 decimal places and no % sign or exponent, compared exactly. Default: 100, the paper's (every sequence with a valid k-mer has the Index).

**References:** Tharanga et al. 2025, Methods, [doi:10.1093/bib/bbae607](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae607)

#### `--hcs-eligible-only`

Build conserved sequences from positions with support above T only, where T is the support threshold of the analysis (recorded in the results); positions with support at most T end a region instead of being flagged.

**References:** Hu et al. 2013, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0059994](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0059994); Castresana 2000, [doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a026334](https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a026334)

#### `-o, --output <PATH>`

Write the conserved sequences here ('-' = standard output, the default). The name gives the format: .json or .tsv, optionally followed by .gz or .zst. A file name with neither gets JSON, with a warning (output\_format\_assumed); standard output and other streams get JSON. A name that asks for JSON Lines, for another compression (.bz2, .xz, ...) or for two, or that is a folder, is refused. -O chooses the format instead. Files are replaced atomically, and never the input.

#### `-O, --output-format <FORMAT>`

Format of -o: 'json' (regions with their members and provenance) or 'tsv' (one row per region). Default: from the file extension; a file name without one gets JSON, with a warning, and standard output gets JSON. Must agree with the file extension.

- Values:
  - `json`: Regions with members and provenance
  - `tsv`: One row per region

#### `--pretty`

Indent JSON output

Global options (`--color`, `-q`, `-v`) and `-h`/`--help`, `-V`/`--version` apply to every subcommand; see [`dima`](#dima).

## `dima cite`

Print how to cite DiMA (and, with --from, the references of a run)

```text
dima cite [OPTIONS]
```

### Options

#### `--format <FORMAT>`

Output format

- Values:
  - `text`: Plain text
  - `bibtex`: BibTeX
  - `ris`: RIS
  - `cff`: Citation File Format (CITATION.cff)
- Default: `text`

#### `--from <FILE>`

Results of a run, and/or the conserved sequences computed from them (give the option twice; '-' reads standard input): print a methods text and the references of the methods used, or with --format bibtex, ris or cff the references only. Both files must come from one run: conserved sequences of another input, k or T are refused

Global options (`--color`, `-q`, `-v`) and `-h`/`--help`, `-V`/`--version` apply to every subcommand; see [`dima`](#dima).

## `dima completions`

Print a shell completion script

```text
dima completions [OPTIONS] <SHELL>
```

### Options

#### `<SHELL>`

The shell

- Values:
  - `bash`
  - `elvish`
  - `fish`
  - `powershell`
  - `zsh`

Global options (`--color`, `-q`, `-v`) and `-h`/`--help`, `-V`/`--version` apply to every subcommand; see [`dima`](#dima).

## `dima help`

Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

```text
dima help [COMMAND]
```

Global options (`--color`, `-q`, `-v`) and `-h`/`--help`, `-V`/`--version` apply to every subcommand; see [`dima`](#dima).
